name: Glutamic acid
text:
Glutamic acid is one of the amino acids that make up proteins. In its free form it is responsible for the savoury taste known as umami, and it occurs naturally in foods such as cheese, soy sauce and tomatoes.

For food use the L-form is obtained by fermentation or by hydrolysis of proteins such as wheat gluten. It is used as a flavour enhancer, although glutamate is more often added in the form of its sodium salt, monosodium glutamate (E621).

name: Monosodium glutamate
text:
Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is the sodium salt of glutamic acid. Glutamate occurs naturally in foods such as tomatoes, cheese and kombu seaweed; MSG was first isolated in 1908 by the Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda, who was studying the savoury taste of kombu.

Today it is made mainly by bacterial fermentation of carbohydrates from sugar beet, sugar cane, tapioca or molasses. It adds umami taste to stock cubes, soups, ramen, gravies, condiments and savoury snacks.

Blinded studies have not shown the headaches and other symptoms popularly attributed to MSG when it is eaten with food in normal amounts.

name: Monopotassium glutamate
text:
Monopotassium glutamate is the potassium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid.

It is used as a flavour enhancer that gives a savoury umami taste, and serves as a sodium-free alternative to monosodium glutamate (E621).

name: Calcium diglutamate
text:
Calcium diglutamate is a calcium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid present in protein-containing foods. It can be prepared by reacting glutamic acid with calcium carbonate.

It is a flavour enhancer. Because the glutamate is what carries the taste, it gives the same savoury umami effect as monosodium glutamate (E621) without adding sodium.

name: Monoammonium glutamate
text:
Monoammonium glutamate is the ammonium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid.

It is used as a flavour enhancer that gives a savoury umami taste, like the other salts of glutamic acid such as monosodium glutamate (E621).

name: Magnesium diglutamate
text:
Magnesium diglutamate is a magnesium salt of glutamic acid, an amino acid.

It is used as a flavour enhancer that gives a savoury umami taste, like the other salts of glutamic acid such as monosodium glutamate (E621).

name: Guanylic acid
text:
Guanylic acid (guanosine monophosphate) is a nucleotide, one of the building blocks of RNA. It was first identified as the umami substance in dried shiitake mushrooms and occurs in a number of other mushrooms. Commercially it is produced by microbial fermentation.

It is a flavour enhancer that provides umami taste, but it is mostly used in the form of its salts, such as disodium guanylate (E627). Being fairly expensive, these are usually combined with glutamates.

name: Disodium guanylate
text:
Disodium guanylate is the sodium salt of guanylic acid (E626), a nucleotide first identified as the umami substance of dried shiitake mushrooms. It is produced mainly by bacterial fermentation.

It is a fairly expensive flavour enhancer, so it is usually used together with monosodium glutamate or another glutamate source, and often with disodium inosinate. Typical products are instant noodles, crisps and other snacks, savoury rice, tinned vegetables, cured meats and packet soups.

JECFA has noted that large intakes of guanylates and inosinates can raise uric acid levels, which is relevant for people prone to gout.

name: Dipotassium guanylate
text:
Dipotassium guanylate is a potassium salt of guanylic acid (E626), a nucleotide that is one of the building blocks of RNA.

It is used as a flavour enhancer to provide umami taste. Like the other guanylates, it is usually combined with glutamates.

name: Calcium guanylate
text:
Calcium guanylate is the calcium salt of guanylic acid (E626), a nucleotide present in all living cells as part of RNA.

It is used as a flavour enhancer that provides umami taste.

name: Inosinic acid
text:
Inosinic acid (inosine monophosphate) is a nucleotide that occurs naturally in meat and fish. For food use it is made by fermentation of sugars or obtained from animal products.

It is a flavour enhancer for umami taste, although its salts, such as disodium inosinate (E631), are the forms usually used. Inosinates act in synergy with glutamates and are mostly used in soups, sauces and seasonings to intensify and balance meaty flavour.

name: Disodium inosinate
text:
Disodium inosinate is the sodium salt of inosinic acid (E630), a nucleotide found naturally in meat and fish. Large-scale production is now mainly by bacterial fermentation, although it can also be prepared from animal products.

It is a relatively expensive flavour enhancer that works in synergy with monosodium glutamate or other glutamate sources, and is often combined with disodium guanylate (as E635).

JECFA has noted that large intakes of inosinates and guanylates can raise uric acid levels, which is relevant for people prone to gout.

name: Dipotassium inosinate
text:
Dipotassium inosinate is a potassium salt of inosinic acid (E630), a nucleotide found naturally in meat and fish.

Like the other inosinates, it is a flavour enhancer that intensifies umami taste and is mostly used in soups, sauces and seasonings.

name: Calcium inosinate
text:
Calcium inosinate is a calcium salt of inosinic acid (E630), a nucleotide found naturally in meat and fish.

Like the other inosinates, it is a flavour enhancer that intensifies umami taste and is mostly used in soups, sauces and seasonings.

name: Calcium 5'-ribonucleotides
text:
Calcium 5'-ribonucleotides are a mixture of the calcium salts of the nucleotides inosinic acid and guanylic acid.

The mixture is used as a flavour enhancer. On their own these compounds have little taste, but combined with glutamates such as monosodium glutamate they strongly boost umami.

name: Disodium 5'-ribonucleotides
text:
Disodium 5'-ribonucleotides are a mixture of disodium inosinate (E631) and disodium guanylate (E627), the sodium salts of the nucleotides inosinic acid and guanylic acid. Large-scale production is mainly by bacterial fermentation.

The mixture works in synergy with glutamates: a blend of 98% monosodium glutamate and 2% of this mixture has about four times the flavour-enhancing power of monosodium glutamate alone. It is mainly used in flavoured noodles, snack foods, crisps, crackers, sauces and fast food.

JECFA evaluated it in 1974 and again in 1993 and did not consider a numerical acceptable daily intake necessary.

name: Maltol
text:
Maltol is a naturally occurring organic compound with a caramel-like odour. It is found in the bark of larch trees and the needles of pine trees, and it forms when malt is roasted, which gives it its name, and when bread is baked.

It is used mainly as a flavour enhancer and to give foods a pleasant aroma, and it is also used in perfumes, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.

name: Ethyl maltol
text:
Ethyl maltol is an organic compound closely related to maltol (E636), with an ethyl group in place of maltol's methyl group. It is a white solid with a sweet smell often described as caramelised sugar or caramelised fruit.

It is a common flavouring in confectionery and is widely used in other foods, as well as in perfumes, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.

name: Glycine and its sodium salt
text:
Glycine is the simplest stable amino acid and one of the building blocks of proteins. The body makes it, and it is also obtained from the diet. For food use it is produced by chemical synthesis. This additive number also covers its sodium salt.

In food it serves as a flavour enhancer: glycine is mildly sweet, which gave it its name from the Greek word for sweet, and it counters the aftertaste of saccharin. It also has some preservative properties.

name: L-leucine
text:
L-leucine is an essential amino acid: the body cannot make it, so it must come from the diet, mainly from protein-containing foods such as meat, dairy products, soy products, beans and other legumes.

As a food additive it is classed as a flavour enhancer; in the EU its listed use is in table-top sweeteners in tablet form. Leucine is also sold as a dietary supplement.

name: Zinc acetate
text:
Zinc acetate is the zinc salt of acetic acid, a colourless solid that commonly occurs as the dihydrate.

As a food additive it is classed as a flavour enhancer and is used in chewing gum. Zinc acetate is also used in dietary supplements and in some lozenges for the common cold.
